title: The Sound Effects Department
clue: Every good comic needs a CRUNCH, a SQUEAK and a THUMP.
reveal: Open a tiny sound stage for your dog: three safe things that make noises when they investigate them. Whatever your dog makes happen becomes a panel in a comic page, with the sound effect lettered large.
objective: Let your dog trigger three gentle sound effects at their own pace, then turn the best three moments into comic panels.
instructions: Make a stage on a non-slip floor with three stations, a few steps apart: a flat clean paper bag (handles removed) to crinkle, a squeaky toy they already know, and a soft ball to bounce on a folded blanket. Leave out any station you think may worry your dog.
Add a mat with water to one side as the dressing room. Keep your voice low and let your dog come when they like.

Sit back and let them wander the stage for five to ten minutes. Each time they cause a sound, jot the sound on a card in your own words: CRINKLE, SQUEAK, THUD. Also jot sounds they make naturally: a sigh, a jingle, a nail click, a tail thump.
If they ignore a station, swap its spot once. If a sound makes them back away, take it away and note that too. Never squeak, crinkle or push the toy at them.
Choose three favorites and take a quick photo or sketch of the moment, or draw it afterwards from memory.
Lay the three panels in a row on a sheet of paper and letter each sound effect big and bold beside its panel. Add a thought bubble if you like.
Read the page aloud softly and tidy the stage, leaving the toy for them.
twist: Your dog is the sound designer: they decide which sounds exist by what they choose to investigate, and you only letter them.
variations: Quiet version: use only natural sounds (sigh, tag jingle, tail thump) during a nap or settle.
For a sound-sensitive dog: skip the paper bag and squeaker and use a plush toy and soft ball on a blanket.
For limited mobility: make one station beside the bed and work from a chair.
For a puppy: one station, two minutes, then a nap.
completion: Your dog has had a go at the stage and you have three lettered panels.
photoIdea: Your dog mid-investigation at their favorite station, taken from low and without calling them. Each panel can be a natural moment.
memoryPrompt: Which sound effect did your dog earn, and how did you spell it?
safety: Take away paper or toys they start to tear or swallow, and supervise throughout.
Never squeak, crinkle or shake things at them. If a sound worries them, remove it.
One dog on the stage at a time so no toy gets guarded.
